polarisation calibration should be applied in any lidar system that is intended to be used for quantitative measurements of linear depolarisation ratios.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polarisation calibration can be done with the same accuracy as the calibration for the total signal, if the polarising optics of the lidar is well aligned.

the polarisation calibration is an indispensable tool for the determination of aerosol optical properties from lidar signals and for the correction of systematic errors caused, e.g., by non-ideal optics.

The main takeaway from our work is that
polarisation effects are not negligible for lidar systems with low signal-to-noise ratios, such as for Raman lidars.

the polarisation calibration is not an independent measurement of the state of the polarisation of the backscattered light, but that it is a measurement of the state-of-polarisation of the backscatter signal in the lidar system, which is a function of the polarisation properties of the optical elements of the system.

the polarisation calibration of a lidar can be performed by measuring only two signals, and that the calibration can be performed in the presence of polarising optics, which can be useful for the calibration of field-deployed lidar systems.
